name: Short stature due to growth hormone qualitative anomaly

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Growth Hormone Qualitative Deficiency Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Short stature defined as height below the 3rd percentile for age and sex
Normal or near-normal serum growth hormone levels with impaired biological activity
Reduced serum insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) levels despite normal GH secretion
Exclusion of other causes of short stature including GH deficiency and systemic diseases

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of short stature with normal GH levels but reduced GH bioactivity and low IGF-1 levels, excluding other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Functional assays to assess GH bioactivity are essential for diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Disproportionate short stature with normal GH serum concentration
searchTerms: short height with normal growth hormone

pathognomonic.symptomName: Low serum insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) levels despite normal GH secretion
searchTerms: low IGF-1 despite normal growth hormone
growth factor deficiency with normal GH

common.symptomName: Delayed bone age relative to chronological age
searchTerms: slow bone growth compared to age

common.symptomName: Reduced growth velocity below expected norms
Mild facial dysmorphism including frontal bossing
Increased adiposity with normal muscle mass
searchTerms: increased body fat with normal muscles
low blood sugar episodes in infancy
pituitary gland looks smaller than normal

laboratory: Low serum IGF-1 and IGFBP-3 levels
Reduced GH bioactivity in functional assays
imaging: Delayed bone age on hand/wrist X-ray
Occasionally hypoplastic pituitary gland on MRI
other: Exclusion of systemic diseases causing short stature

distinguishingFeatures: Poor response to GH stimulation tests
Low IGF-1 with low or normal GH levels

redFlags: Signs of systemic illness or chronic disease
references: Orphanet: Short stature due to growth hormone qualitative anomaly, ORPHA:629
Cianfarani S, et al. Growth hormone qualitative defects: clinical and molecular aspects. Horm Res. 2002.
Rosenfeld RG. Growth hormone deficiency and insensitivity. Pediatr Endocrinol Rev. 2007.
